title: Asian Stocks Slide After US Tech Rout, Bonds Rally: Markets Wrap
summary: Asian stocks extended losses, tracking declines on Wall Street as investors rotated out of technology giants following a blistering rally earlier this year and sought safety in Treasuries and currencies such as the yen.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 23
summary: Brent oil headed for a third weekly gain as intensifying attacks on Saudi Arabia raised the risk of wider Middle East supply disruptions.

title: Yen Jumps as Traders Seek Safety Amid Global Flight From Risk
summary: The yen extended its gains on Friday, outperforming all its major counterparts, as a selloff in global equities boosted demand for havens.

title: Japan Inflation Rises Above BOJ Target Level, Backing Rate Hikes
summary: Japan’s key price gauge rose above the Bank of Japan’s target level for the first time this year, supporting the case for a widely expected BOJ interest rate hike in December.

title: Australia’s Victoria State Approves $700 Million Gas Project
summary: Australia’s Victoria state has approved the production license for a A$1 billion ($700 million) natural gas project to help avoid a forecast gas shortage.

title: Treasuries Surge as Worldwide Worries Spark Rush to Safety
summary: Treasuries rallied for their best day in more than two years, surging across the board as a deepening rout in AI-related shares, market turmoil in France and fresh Mideast tensions all combined to make US government debt the investment of choice for anxious traders.

title: Australian Growth Likely Slower Than Expected, Chalmers Says
summary: Australia’s growth will likely be slower than the 1.75% forecast in May’s budget, Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers said Friday, as a series of rate hikes and rising inflation start to bite on the economy.

title: What a 35-Hour Train Ride Reveals About Vietnam’s Future
summary: Vietnam is betting big on a $65 billion high-speed railway linking Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. Construction is set to start in late 2027 and take at least a decade to complete. The line could cut the roughly 35-hour journey to just six hours. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: New York City Bans Horse-Drawn Carriages After Decade-Long Battle
summary: New York’s City Council voted to ban horse-drawn carriages, ending a Central Park tourist staple dating to the 19th century after years of debate over the horses’ place on city streets. Bloomberg's  Laura Nahmias explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rio Tinto to Spend $1.9 Billion on Australian Bauxite Expansion
summary: Rio Tinto Group will spend $1.9 billion to expand its bauxite mining operations in northern Australia, with the development of a new major mine to replace production from depleting projects.

title: Typhoon Champi Shuts Taiwan’s $5 Trillion Stock Market
summary: Taiwan’s stock exchange will shut Friday as Typhoon Champi approaches the island, bringing heavy rainfall and strong winds that prompted authorities to shut offices and schools in the capital city of Taipei.

title: BlackRock's Senra on Investment Shifts, Wealth Transfer
summary: Armando Senra, Head of the Americas Institutional Business at BlackRock, said family offices generally view geopolitical tensions as a source of short-term market and allocation effects, rather than a reason for major long-term portfolio changes. He said investors are attentive to current events but are maintaining broader trends seen among institutional clients: expanding private-market exposure with greater diversification and using ETFs for both active and index strategies. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Mickey Drexler on Decker Results and Retail Outlook
summary: Mickey Drexler, Chair of Alex Mill and Former CEO and chair of J. Crew, tells Bloomberg that apparel retailers need to do more to give consumers a reason to buy. He says product, discounting and especially newness matter, while arguing that fashion has put too little emphasis on creativity and reinvention. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Affirm, Sam’s Club Strike Exclusive Buy Now, Pay Later Deal
summary: Affirm is teaming up with Walmart’s Sam’s Club as the retailer’s exclusive buy-now, pay-later partner, just weeks before the key holiday shopping season kicks off. Affirm will serve as Sam’s Club’s exclusive BNPL provider in a multi-year agreement, starting in that role on Sam’s Club’s website in the coming weeks and rolling out to stores in 2027, according to a statement Thursday that didn’t disclose terms of the deal. Max Levchin, Founder & CEO of Affirm, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Kroger CFO: We Are an Agent for the Consumer
summary: Kroger CFO David Kennerley discusses the company plans to invest $5 billion in consumer value, including affordable groceries and simpler promotions, while seeking to fund the effort through $4 billion in structural cost savings. Kennerley said the company is seeing a slight uptick in inflation but remains within the range it projected earlier in the year, and will accept supplier price increases only when justified. He speaks with Romaine Bostick in "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Huntington Bancshares CEO Stephen Steinour on 3Q Results
summary: Huntington Bank shares were little changed after the company reported revenue below expectations and earnings per share in line. CEO Steve Steinour said the results reinforce confidence in meeting financial targets and delivering sustained earnings growth. He cited growth and the integration of the Cadence and Veritex partnerships, while explaining that stronger competition has made some lending unattractive. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: A Tesla-SpaceX Merger Doesn’t Add Up
summary: Elon Musk is eager to consolidate Tesla and SpaceX, but recent earnings numbers show how odd that merger would be, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Liam Denning says. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: TD Cowen Analyst on Chipotle Downgrade
summary: Andrew Charles discusses TD Cowen’s downgrade of Chipotle to Hold, citing concerns about sales trends. He said the company’s recent same-store sales have benefited from creative campaigns, including four annual limited-time protein offerings, value initiatives and a new chief marketing officer, but he expected these efforts to deliver stronger results in the fourth quarter and argued that growth will become harder in 2027 as Chipotle laps those drivers and must rely on less-proven initiatives. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Jane Street, HRT Are Spending Billions to Win in AI Era
summary: High-frequency trading firms are even building their own data centers as they compete for an edge in the AI era.

title: Stocks Fall as AI Jitters Ease Bets on Fed Hikes: Markets Wrap
summary: Wall Street shunned stocks as a technology rout and Middle East risks drove investors to the safety of bonds, reducing bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike in 2026.
